title: RFC 3986 URI Normalization Test Corpus
profile: Absolute HTTP/HTTPS URIs. RFC 3986 sections 6.2.2.1, 6.2.2.2, 6.2.2.3 (incl. 5.2.4), and 6.2.3. Normalization only.

in_scope: Syntax validation needed to decide 'normalize or reject' for an absolute http/https URI
out_of_scope_tested_elsewhere: BDEW 3.3: Hash(URI), Hash(Payload), Hash(creationDateTime), Hash(transactionId), Hash(initialTransactionId)
Concatenation M = Hash(URI) + Hash(Payload) + ... (including the optional initialTransactionId rule)
ECDSA / SHA-256 computation, TR-03111 Plain encoding of the signature
RFC 8785 JSON canonicalization of the payload
HTTP headers X-BDEW-SIGNATURE, X-BDEW-DIGEST, X-BDEW-CERT; RFC 4648 Base64; RFC 9440 certificate encoding
Building the absolute URI from an HTTP request (Host header, TLS, proxies, request-target forms)
Query-parameter semantics (parsing, sorting, de-duplication, required parameters)
UTF-8 byte conversion of the normalized string before hashing
RFC 3986 6.2.1 (simple string comparison) and 6.2.4 / 6.2.5 (protocol-based normalization, DNS, redirects)
Any HTTP-level business rule (resource existence, case sensitivity of server resources)

assumptions: A1: Input is ONE absolute http/https URI string, exactly as it will be hashed. The normalizer does not trim, does not percent-encode raw characters, does not convert IRIs/IDN and does not repair anything.
A2: Any input that is not a syntactically valid absolute http/https URI (RFC 3986 ABNF) is rejected (error/exception). No best-effort output.

A3: Order of operations: (1) validate + split into components, (2) percent-encoding normalization of ALL components (decode unreserved, uppercase remaining hex), (3) lowercase scheme and host (never touching percent triplets), (4) remove_dot_segments on the PATH only, (5) scheme-based normalization. Consequence: '%2e%2e' is decoded to '..' before step 4 and is therefore removed as a dot segment.
A4: Dot-segment removal applies to the path only. Query, fragment, userinfo and host are never subject to it (RFC 5.2.4 note on '/../' and '/./' in queries).
A5: Percent-decoding is single-pass and left-to-right; the result of a decode is never re-scanned (%2541 stays %2541).
A6: Only unreserved characters are decoded. Reserved characters (gen-delims and sub-delims) and all other octets stay encoded; %2F is never treated as a path separator.

A7: Scheme-based normalization is implemented for http (default port 80) and https (default port 443) only. Empty path becomes '/' when an authority is present (also when only a query and/or fragment follows). Empty ':' port and default port are removed.
A8: Delimiters of empty components are preserved: '?', '#', and the '@' / ':' of empty userinfo. Only the empty-port ':' is removed.

A9: The fragment is preserved (with percent-normalization applied). RFC 6.2.3: 'a' and 'a#' are different. If an upstream component strips the fragment before the normalizer is called, move section 05 fragment tests out of scope.

A10: Nothing beyond RFC 3986 6.2.2 / 6.2.3 is allowed: no query sorting/dedup, no trailing-slash handling, no '+'<->'%20', no IPv6 compression, no host trailing-dot removal, no Unicode normalization, no DNS/IDN conversion.
A11: Output is ASCII. Conversion of the normalized URI to bytes, hashing, concatenation (M), signing and header handling happen elsewhere.

A12: Tests with 'policy': true or in 09_policy_decisions encode a RECOMMENDED decision where RFC 3986 is silent; tests with requires=generic_scheme_support need non-HTTP scheme support and may be skipped otherwise.
A13: Tests flagged 'generated': true are produced by a rule (exhaustive 0x00-0xFF octet sweep) rather than written by hand.
recommended_order: invalid_inputs (the normalizer must refuse before it normalizes)

test_format.valid_case: {id, input, expected, purpose, rfc?, policy?, alternative?, requires?, generated?} -> normalize(input) must equal expected
test_format.invalid_case: {id, input, expected_outcome: 'reject', reason, rfc?, policy?} -> normalize(input) must signal an error
test_format.equivalence_group: all members must normalize to expected_common
test_format.distinct_pair: normalize(a) must differ from normalize(b); both inputs are valid

sections.description: RFC 3986 6.2.2.1: lowercase scheme and host; uppercase the hex digits of every percent triplet (all components). Every other component is case-sensitive and must be left untouched.

tests.purpose: Punycode label is only lowercased, never converted.
IPv6: only case is normalized; no zero compression (not an RFC 3986 rule).
Lowercase hex in path triplet -> uppercase.

UTF-8 octets stay encoded, hex uppercased.
Host lowercasing must NOT lowercase the hex digits of a retained triplet.
Non-reserved, non-unreserved octets: only hex case changes.
Path case preserved while triplet is uppercased.

sections.description: RFC 3986 6.2.2.2 + 2.3: decode percent-encoded octets that are ASCII unreserved characters (ALPHA / DIGIT / '-' / '.' / '_' / '~'). Everything else stays encoded (hex uppercased). Decoding is single-pass. Applies to every component. Includes an exhaustive 0x00-0xFF sweep for path and query.

sections.description: RFC 3986 6.2.2.3 + 5.2.4: apply remove_dot_segments to the PATH only. Only COMPLETE segments '.' and '..' count. Query, fragment, userinfo and host are never touched. Percent-encoded dots (%2e) are decoded first (assumption A3), while %2F never acts as a separator. For absolute paths steps 2A and 2D of 5.2.4 cannot be reached; steps 2B, 2C, 2E are covered.

'b.' removed as a whole segment by '..'.
'..;x' (path parameter) is not a dot segment.
Segment with path parameter removed by '..'.

Encoded slash is not a separator: 'a%2F..' is one segment.
Encoded slashes around '..' stay literal; hex uppercased.

sections.description: RFC 3986 6.2.3 for http/https: empty path -> '/'; empty port or default port (http:80, https:443) removed together with ':'; non-default ports kept; delimiters of empty query / fragment / userinfo are kept.

tests.purpose: 443 is NOT the default for http.
80 is NOT the default for https.
Empty query delimiter is kept; path becomes '/'.

Empty userinfo: '@' delimiter is significant, keep.

sections.description: Guard against over-normalization. These inputs are already in normal form; the normalizer must return them byte-for-byte. Anything RFC 3986 6.2.2/6.2.3 does not license must NOT happen (no sorting, no trailing-slash changes, no '+'/%20 conversion, no encoding of raw reserved characters, ...).

tests.purpose: No trailing slash is added to a non-empty path.
Trailing slash kept on nested path.

Raw sub-delims / ':' / '@' in path are NOT encoded.
Raw sub-delims / '/' / '?' in query are NOT encoded.
Raw sub-delims / '/' / '?' in fragment are NOT encoded.
Query parameter order is kept (no sorting).
Empty values and value-less keys are kept.
Keys differing only by case kept distinct.

sections.description: Interaction of several rules in one URI; checks the order of operations (decode -> case-fold -> dot removal -> scheme-based).

tests.purpose: Decoding creates dot segments, which are then removed.
Empty port + dots in path only.
Encoded traversal payload is neutralized but kept (no decoding of %2F).

sections.description: Examples quoted verbatim in RFC 3986 6.2.2 and 6.2.3 (where the RFC uses a non-HTTP scheme, the test is marked requires=generic_scheme_support and may be skipped by an HTTP/HTTPS-only normalizer).

tests.purpose: RFC 6.2.3: 'http://example.com/?' is NOT equivalent to the four above.

sections.description: Large / adversarial inputs for the normalizer itself (no recursion limits, no quadratic blow-up, no state leakage).

RFC 3986 is silent or ambiguous here. The expected value encodes the RECOMMENDED decision; 'alternative' names the other defensible behaviour. Decide once, document it, and keep both signer and verifier identical.

tests.purpose: Port '0080' has the VALUE 80 = scheme default -> removed (RFC 3.2.3 speaks of the port's value).
Leading zeros on a NON-default port: no RFC rule strips them.
Out-of-range port is syntactically valid (*DIGIT); range checks are not normalization.
Port 0 is syntactically valid and not a default.

Raw double quote is not allowed in a path; must be percent-encoded.

Raw '>' is not allowed in a path; must be percent-encoded.

Raw '|' is not allowed in a path; must be percent-encoded.
Raw '}' is not allowed in a path; must be percent-encoded.
Raw '[' / ']' are only allowed in an IP literal host.

Encoded vs raw unreserved characters in every component.

properties.name: idempotence
properties.statement: normalize(normalize(x)) == normalize(x) for every valid input in this file.

properties.name: fixed_point
properties.statement: Every 'expected' value is itself a valid input and normalizes to itself.

properties.name: ascii_only
properties.statement: Output of every valid input contains only ASCII characters (no raw non-ASCII is ever produced).

properties.name: no_uppercase_scheme_or_host
properties.statement: Output scheme and host contain no uppercase letters outside percent triplets.

properties.name: triplets_uppercase
properties.statement: Every percent triplet in the output uses uppercase hex digits.

properties.name: no_encoded_unreserved
properties.statement: No output triplet encodes an unreserved character.

properties.name: no_dot_segments_in_path
properties.statement: Output path contains no complete '.' or '..' segment.

properties.name: length_non_increasing_except_root
properties.statement: Output is never longer than input except for (a) adding '/' for an empty path. Percent normalization and dot removal only shrink; hex-case changes keep the length.

properties.name: determinism
properties.statement: Repeated calls with the same input give the same output; no global/state leakage between calls.

properties.name: reject_is_total
properties.statement: Every input in invalid_inputs is rejected; none is silently repaired and none returns a partially normalized string.
